competition.title: Competitions
competition.prizeDisclaimer: The client provides and pays for the prize and is responsible for any tax, payroll or legal implications.

masteryMonth.name: Mastery Month
masteryMonth.howToWin: Master the most modules in the period. A module is mastered when you have answered every question in it correctly at least once. Retakes are welcome.
masteryMonth.why: It rewards real knowledge. Trying again is encouraged, not penalised, and speed does not matter.

knowledgeBuilder.name: Knowledge Builder
knowledgeBuilder.howToWin: Answer correctly the most different questions in the period.
knowledgeBuilder.why: It rewards the amount of correct learning, and repeating the same quiz does not help.

learningStreak.name: Learning Streak Challenge
learningStreak.howToWin: Be active in the most weeks in the period. A week counts when you complete at least one lesson or quiz.
learningStreak.why: It encourages little-and-often learning that suits shift work. Each week counts once, and holidays or sickness do not wipe out your progress.

teamShowdown.name: Team Showdown
teamShowdown.howToWin: Teams or sites compete on the percentage of their assigned training completed before the due date.
teamShowdown.why: Percentages are fair to teams and sites of different sizes, a shared goal builds support, and no individual is ranked.

beatTheExpiry.name: Beat the Expiry
beatTheExpiry.howToWin: Complete a refresher before it expires, within the window, to be entered into a random draw. Refreshers done outside the app count once the certificate is approved.
beatTheExpiry.why: It rewards keeping up to date, not speed.

completeAndWin.name: Complete and Win
completeAndWin.howToWin: Complete and pass the chosen modules by the end date to be entered into a random draw.
completeAndWin.why: Everyone who qualifies has an equal chance, so there is no reason to race. It suits must-do training such as the September framework update.

scenarioSavvy.name: Scenario Savvy
scenarioSavvy.howToWin: Choose the best outcome in the most scenario questions. Each question counts once.
scenarioSavvy.why: It rewards good judgement, which is what inspectors want staff to show.

closedBook.name: Closed-Book Challenge
closedBook.howToWin: Answer correctly the most different questions in closed-book mode in the period.
closedBook.why: It rewards recall without notes. Notes are locked in counted attempts. Open-book attempts are still available, they just do not count here.

mustDo.question: How do I see what I must complete?
mustDo.answer: Open Home. Next up lists the training you need to do, with due dates. Overdue items show first. When Home says You are compliant, nothing is outstanding.

renewals.question: How do renewals work?
renewals.answer: Some training runs out after a set time, like a safeguarding refresher. Coming up on Home shows what runs out soon. Do the refresher before the date.

xp.question: What are XP and levels?
xp.answer: XP are points you earn for learning, like finishing a lesson or passing a quiz. XP moves you up levels and earns badges. Going fast earns nothing extra.

notes.question: How do notes work?
notes.answer: You can write private notes on any lesson. Only you can see them. Notes are locked while you take a closed-book quiz, and you can see them again afterwards.

closedBook.question: What is a closed-book quiz?
closedBook.answer: In a closed-book quiz you cannot open your notes or the lessons until you have finished. It checks what you remember. Your results are saved as normal.

leaderboards.question: How do leaderboards work, and can I hide myself?
leaderboards.answer: Leaderboards show progress in friendly competitions. They never rank people by how fast they are. You can hide yourself from a leaderboard in Me, under Privacy.

textSize.question: How do I change the text size?
textSize.answer: Open Me, then Display and accessibility. Choose a bigger text size and you will see the change straight away. You can also switch on dark mode or high contrast there.

cannotLogIn.question: What should I do if I cannot log in?
cannotLogIn.answer: Check your PIN or password and try again. If it still does not work, ask your manager to reset it. They can do this in a moment.

upload.question: How do I add a certificate from a course I did elsewhere?
upload.answer: Open the training and choose Upload a certificate. Add a photo or PDF and the date you finished. Your manager checks it and you get a message.

reportMistake.question: I think there is a mistake in a question. What can I do?
reportMistake.answer: Choose Report a problem under the question. Say what looks wrong. Your manager sees it, and mistakes in provider training are fixed for everyone.

inviteStaff.question: How do I add staff and invite them?
inviteStaff.answer: Open People, then Add people. Enter their name, job role and email. They get an invitation and choose a PIN when they first sign in.

publishModule.question: How do I create and publish a module?
publishModule.answer: Open Modules, then New module. Paste your lessons and questions, check the preview on the phone frame, and fix anything the publish checklist lists. Then choose Publish.

categories.question: How do I use categories and groups?
categories.answer: Categories help staff find training. Groups bundle several modules so you can give them out together, for example a new starter set. Manage both under Modules.

autoAssign.question: How do I assign training and set up auto-assign rules?
autoAssign.answer: Choose Assign to give training to chosen people. Under Rules, auto-assign rules do it for you, for example when a new person joins.

competitions.question: How do I run a competition and choose prizes?
competitions.answer: Open Competitions and choose a template. Set the dates, who can join and a prize. Competitions reward learning and never reward speed. Add a prize before you publish.

themes.question: How do I change our theme?
themes.answer: Open Themes and pick a ready-made theme or build your own. Colours are checked so text stays readable. You can schedule a theme and preview it as staff.

sitesRoles.question: How do sites and roles work?
sitesRoles.answer: Each site has its own people. Roles decide what each admin can do, and you can limit an admin to one site. Change them under Team and roles.

inspectorExport.question: How do I produce an inspector-ready export?
inspectorExport.answer: Open Reports, then Exports, and choose the inspector-ready pack. You get training records and dates for the people and period you choose.

billing.question: Where do I find plan and billing details?
billing.answer: Open Plan and billing to see your plan, invoices and add-ons. You need permission to view billing. If you cannot see it, ask the Account Owner.

twoStep.question: What is two-step sign-in?
twoStep.answer: It asks for a code from an authenticator app as well as your password. Every admin needs it. Keep your recovery codes somewhere safe.

calendarReminders.title: Calendar and reminders
calendarReminders.body: The calendar shows your training dates in one place, and you can add them to your phone. Reminders now arrive a few days before something is due.

aiAssistant.what: Explains a quiz answer in simple words when someone asks, using only the lesson and the official source.
aiAssistant.example: A new starter is unsure why a baby must sleep in a cot. They tap Explain and get a short, plain answer.

translation.what: Shows lessons and questions in other languages, marked as machine translated until someone checks them.
translation.example: A cook who reads Polish more easily can read the food allergy module in Polish.

reminders.what: Sends reminders by text message or WhatsApp as well as in the app.
reminders.example: A bank practitioner gets a text two days before their safeguarding refresher is due.

extraContentPack.what: Adds a second industry pack of ready-made training.
extraContentPack.example: A nursery group that also runs a cafe adds the hospitality pack.

onboarding.what: Our team sets up your account, loads your people and applies your branding.
onboarding.example: A group of eight nurseries has all its staff, teams and sites set up before the first day.
